points.reason: The process resets key_mem and conditionally overwrites a selected key word, so the key can be cleared, changed, or prevented from being programmed, but this block does not itself read the key out.
tmp_z carries a selected key word into the XTEA arithmetic, but the RTL shows no direct observation, unauthorized modification, or blocking mechanism at this internal computation point.
tmp_r combines the key-derived value with other XTEA operands as normal computation and has no direct external observation or control of key storage.
xtea_core uses the key-derived arithmetic result to compute XTEA output, but the RTL does not expose or modify the key itself at this computation point.
result_select releases an XTEA result selected by the instruction controls; dependence of that result on the key is normal behavior and does not expose the key itself.
The concurrent assignment directly returns the key_mem word selected by csr_addr_i on csr_rdata_o.
xtea_core captures rs1_i and rs2_i into xtea.opa and xtea.opb and uses those values in the returned XTEA computation; reset or a changed capture condition can alter the stored operands.
tmp_a carries one selected captured operand into the XTEA arithmetic, so its value contributes to the operand-dependent result.
tmp_b carries the other selected captured operand into the result computation.
tmp_x carries a shifted form of a captured operand into the XTEA arithmetic.

points.reason: tmp_r combines operand-derived terms into the value used to compute the XTEA result.
result_select places the operand-dependent xtea.res value on result_o for the consuming processor.
xtea_core stores xtea.res, computes it from tmp_b and tmp_r, and only updates it when xtea.done(0) is asserted; reset or altered arithmetic and gating can clear, corrupt, or prevent the result.
tmp_b is an operand of the result arithmetic, so changing it changes xtea.res, but this internal point does not itself expose or block result availability.
tmp_r is an operand of the xtea.res arithmetic, so changing it corrupts the computed result without directly releasing or blocking it.
result_select releases xtea.res on result_o only for selected operation types and otherwise drives zero and invalid, so its controls can expose, corrupt, or withhold the result.
xtea_core generates and advances xtea.done, while start_i and rtype_i control its assertion; reset or altered control can produce an invalid completion state or prevent completion.
result_select asserts valid_o only for selected instruction types and completion state, so its conditions can falsely assert valid_o or suppress it.
The start_i condition is required before operands are captured and xtea.done is initiated, so suppressing it prevents a new operation from progressing.
csr_we_i gates the key_mem write, so forcing it can replace key material while suppressing it can block required key programming.
csr_addr_i indexes key_mem on a write, so changing it can redirect a key update to a different word.
Although csr_addr_i selects the readback word, this point does not modify the address-selection decision itself and confidentiality is not an objective for this concept.
